segments.title: AI Agents Are Eating Software
segments.question: What must happen before AI agents can be trusted in production systems?
backupQuestions: What is most overhyped about AI agents right now?
Which industries will feel this first — and why?
segments.moderatorNotes: Guide discussion toward reliability and trust. If the group goes broad, bring them back to: what does a human need to hand off a task completely? Watch the time — this topic tends to run long.

segments.title: The Open Source AI Arms Race
segments.question: Does open-sourcing frontier models make the world safer or more dangerous?
backupQuestions: Who actually benefits most when models go open source?
What is the strongest argument for keeping models closed?
Is the open/closed debate even the right frame?
segments.moderatorNotes: This one tends to split the room. Let both sides make their case before synthesizing. Panelist has a strong pro-open position — give the skeptics room first.

segments.title: Vibe Coding: Hype or Paradigm Shift?
segments.question: Will prompt-driven development replace traditional coding skills within a decade?
backupQuestions: What does a senior engineer look like in 2030?
What parts of coding are impossible to prompt your way through?
Is this exciting or terrifying — and why?
segments.moderatorNotes: Audience likely has strong feelings. Let practitioners speak before theorists. Goal: distinguish hype from structural change. Panelist built a production app with 90% AI-generated code.

segments.title: Hardware Hacking for the Curious
segments.question: What is the one piece of hardware knowledge every software developer should have?
backupQuestions: Where do software and hardware assumptions most dangerously diverge?
What project changed how you think about computing?
What barrier is keeping more people out of hardware hacking?
segments.moderatorNotes: Lighter topic — good for post-break energy. Encourage audience members who hack hardware to share. Panelist will likely demo something live; leave space for that.

segments.title: Privacy in the Age of Everything-as-a-Service
segments.question: At what point does convenience cross into surveillance we should refuse?
backupQuestions: Which SaaS tool in your daily stack makes you most uncomfortable — and why do you still use it?
What would a privacy-respecting version of [popular tool] actually look like?
Is individual action on privacy pointless without policy change?
segments.moderatorNotes: This can get political — keep grounded in technical realities. Good to name specific tools and behaviors rather than abstractions. End on something actionable.
